assertions.evidence: The desktop scheduler created the first standalone task at 2026-09-22T00:39:05Z, after the initial checkpoint and independent provider release.
The first task validated the checkpoint, measured provider-r1 READY once, resumed once, received deleteStatus deleted, ran cleanup, and observed AUTONOMOUS_WAKE_OK with measurementCount 2.

A second task was queued at 2026-09-22T00:40:05Z before the first task deleted the automation. It later observed the already-complete checkpoint and performed another provider measurement, raising measurementCount from 2 to 3.
The second task saw checkpoint status complete and did not run resume, cleanup, or create another schedule. completionCount and wakeCount remained 1.

limitations: A successful first task and confirmed schedule deletion do not make a one-minute recurring cadence equivalent to a one-shot wake when another occurrence can already be queued.
The overlapping task changed only measurement accounting, but any post-terminal provider observation violates the fixed one-wake contract.
This failure motivated a daily cadence whose first occurrence is scheduled for the next minute and whose second occurrence is one day later, leaving ample time for terminal self-deletion.
This attempt does not negate the separate durable-pause fallback evidence or establish same-thread heartbeat wake.
